items.title: Deckers’ Sales Growth Slows in First Quarter
items.summary: The footwear and apparel company, which owns the Hoka and Ugg brands, also warned that margins in the current quarter will come under pressure from tariffs and rising freight costs.  Deckers’ sales rose 5.7% in the fiscal first quarter, coming in line with Wall Street’s expectations but slowing from recent periods, including 9.6% growth in the previous quarter.  The slowdown was driven by more moderate growth for Hoka, coming in at 7.7% compared to recent double-digit gains.

items.title: Deckers Outdoor (DECK) Teva Launches Fall 2026 Footwear Push Into Trail Running

The lineup features athlete-led product development, including the new Trailpeak trail running shoe. Teva is expanding its Hurricane and Aventrail franchises across trail running and lifestyle footwear. For Deckers Outdoor, Teva’s Fall 2026 launch highlights its role in performance and outdoor footwear, alongside other brands in the group. items.title: Deckers beats Q1 earnings, raises guidance—but shares dip 3.4%
items.summary: Investing.com -- Deckers Brands (NYSE: DECK) topped $1 billion in first-quarter revenue for the first time in company history, beating Earnings Per Share (EPS) estimates and nudging its full-year profit guidance higher. Despite the record milestone, shares dipped 3.4% following the report as full-year revenue projections slightly trailed Wall Street expectations.
